attempts.label: DANDI:000059
attempts.paper_title: Cooling of Medial Septum Reveals Theta Phase Lag Coordination of Hippocampal Cell Assemblies
attempts.entry_title: Cooling of the medial septum and hippocampal theta coordination (Petersen and Buzsaki 2020)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings hold in this data: cooling the medial septum slows hippocampal theta, raises choice errors (about twofold, where the paper reports threefold) and slows place cell oscillations along with LFP theta. Theta time lags between place cell pairs lengthen, and phase lags stay unchanged only under one reading of the lag. The preserved gap between place cell and LFP theta frequency, and the stable place field size and information, did not hold; the paper drew its fields by hand and they are not shared. Distance-time compression could not be tested, as the paper's surface fit fails on this data and its procedure is not described.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Petersen and Buzsaki (2020) on dandiset 000059, which holds 51 sessions of 5 rats running a figure-8 maze while the medial septum was cooled, with CA1 LFP, curated units, head tracking and the septal temperature. It tests the effects of cooling on theta frequency and power, choice errors, running speed, place cell rates, oscillation frequency, field features, phase precession and the theta time and phase lags of place cell pairs. The hippocampal temperature of the paper's control experiment is not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Theta phase lags between place cell pairs were not affected by MS cooling (P > 0.24 between all conditions).
outcomes.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 3; Figure 5I
outcomes.quote: In contrast, phase lags between spikes of place cell pairs were not affected by MS cooling ( Fig. 5i ; P > 0.24 between all conditions).
outcomes.notes: Lag reading (a), the largest peak within pi of zero: |phase lag| pre against cooling P = 0.37 (8451 pairs), cooling against post P = 0.41, pre against post P = 0.50 (pair reading b: 0.068, 0.084, 0.59). Lag reading (b), the peak nearest zero: pre against cooling P = 2.7e-8 (0.47 against 0.50 rad) and pre against post P = 0.0065. The outcome rests on reading (a); the readings give different outcomes. Without MS13-171130 (theta channel marked bad), lag reading (a) gives P = 0.37, 0.62 and 0.71 (pair reading b, pre against cooling P = 0.040).
deviations: Assumption: the phase lag of a pair is the largest peak of the phase cross-correlogram within pi of zero (lag reading a), the theta-scale lag that the claims file reads for fig5h; the nearest-peak reading (b) picks small side peaks of the smoothed correlogram. The paper does not say which peak (Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression, paragraph 3).

Assumption: fields are found on the map over all trials of an arm, states pooled, so that a field has the same boundaries in every state; the paper does not say on which map (STAR Methods, Place cell analysis).
The lab's theta channel of MS13-171130 is marked bad in the electrodes table; it is used, and the result without that session is shown.

outcomes.statement: The fraction of place cells active in a given theta cycle was not significantly affected by MS cooling (P = 0.2).
outcomes.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 4; Figure 5J
outcomes.quote: we found that the fraction of place cells active in a given theta cycle was not significantly affected by MS cooling ( Fig. 5j ; P = 0.2).
outcomes.notes: Over 82574 theta cycles of 22 sessions with pairs and LFP: fraction of place cells active per cycle 0.189 pre, 0.200 cooling, 0.205 post; rank-sum pre against cooling P = 1.6e-25 (effect +0.011, +5.7%); post against cooling P = 6.6e-10; pre against post P = 4.1e-65. The fraction of all units gives P = 2.2e-38. Cycles share cells and sessions; per-session means (a variant) do not differ from pre to cooling (median change -0.0007, higher in cooling in 9 of 22, signed-rank P = 1.0), the comparison the criterion judges, while post is higher than cooling (P = 0.0029) and pre (P = 0.00059). The criterion fixes the rank-sum over cycles, so the outcome stands; under the per-session variant it would be reproduced.
deviations: Place cells are the cells with a Figure 5 field in the session.

Assumption: fields are found on the map over all trials of an arm, states pooled, so that a field has the same boundaries in every state; the paper does not say on which map (STAR Methods, Place cell analysis).

outcomes.statement: The number of spikes emitted by all neurons per theta cycle was preserved during MS cooling (P > 0.058 between all conditions).
outcomes.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 4; Figure 5K
outcomes.quote: The number of spikes emitted by all neurons per theta cycle was also preserved after MS cooling ( Fig. 5k )
outcomes.notes: Spikes of all curated units per cycle: 30.8 pre, 31.1 cooling, 35.2 post; rank-sum pre against cooling P = 4.9e-7, cooling against post P = 1.8e-39, pre against post P = 5.8e-65. Per-session means (a variant) do not differ from pre to cooling (median change -0.26, signed-rank P = 0.80) but differ from cooling to post (P = 0.0047) and pre to post (P = 0.0059), so the claim of absence fails per session too.
deviations: Assumption: fields are found on the map over all trials of an arm, states pooled, so that a field has the same boundaries in every state; the paper does not say on which map (STAR Methods, Place cell analysis).

outcomes.statement: The waveforms of hippocampal action potentials were not affected by MS cooling.
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 3; Figure S1G
outcomes.quote: Finally, the waveforms of action potentials in the hippocampus ... were not affected by MS cooling ( Suppl. Fig. 1g ).
outcomes.notes: Subset of 4 sessions (MS12-170715, MS13-171130, MS21-180627, MS22-180629), 263 units with at least 20 spikes in both conditions: trough-to-peak latency median 0.80 ms in both, median change +0.05 ms (5.9%), signed-rank P = 1.1e-9 (2 of 4 sessions significant on their own); peak-to-peak amplitude 144.7 against 146.5 uV, median change +0.65 uV (0.7%), P = 0.026. Latency is quantised at 0.05 ms (20 kHz), so the change is one sample. On the mean waveforms interpolated by a cubic spline to 200 kHz, the latency is 0.79 against 0.82 ms, median change +0.035 ms (4.8%), P = 3.1e-11, significant in each of the 4 sessions (P = 9.9e-7 to 0.043). Units have a median of 158 spikes in the control blocks and 115 in the cooling blocks (at least 20 each).
deviations: The dandiset holds no unit waveforms; mean waveforms are measured from the 20 kHz wide-band signal, high-pass 300 Hz, on each unit's largest channel, in two 52 s blocks of pre, three of cooling and two of post per session, on one session per rat (not MS10). The whole wide-band signal (3 TB) does not fit the run.

outcomes.statement: The theta oscillation frequency of putative fast spiking interneurons decreased with MS cooling, as did that of pyramidal cells, by about 14% on average, and pyramidal cells oscillated faster than interneurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 1; Figure S2D
outcomes.quote: Note that pyramidal neurons oscillate faster than interneurons and the theta frequency oscillation of both interneurons and pyramidal cells decreases with MS cooling by approximately 14% on average.
outcomes.notes: Running spikes (above 10 cm/s), cooling against pre: narrow interneurons (145 units with a peak in both states) median 8.93 to 8.40 Hz, decrease 8.7% (median), 6.9% (of the mean), 6.4% (mean of decreases), signed-rank P = 6.4e-13; narrow and wide (191) 8.7%, 6.6%, 5.8%, P = 1.0e-14; pyramidal fields (974) 10.42 to 9.52 Hz, 8.6%, 8.2%, 7.5%; pooled 8.6%, 8.0%, 7.2%. None within 12.6 to 15.4%. Pyramidal cells oscillate faster than interneurons before cooling (10.42 against 8.93 Hz). 116 of 307 interneurons and 249 of 1223 fields have no autocorrelogram peak in a state and are dropped.
deviations: Place fields of Figures 3 and 4 follow the claims file's reading (b), the Figure 5 rule of the Methods (Place cell analysis) with a peak above 10 Hz, as the paper's fields were drawn by hand and the dandiset holds none; fields are drawn on the map over all trials of an arm, states pooled, so that a field has the same boundaries in every state (assumption; the paper does not say on which map). Rate maps use all frames of the trials and a Gaussian smoothing of 1 bin SD (standard choice).
Interneuron spikes are all trial spikes above 10 cm/s ('across the whole maze', Figure S2D).

outcomes.statement: In a control experiment, hippocampal temperature fell by less than 1.5 C at the largest MS temperature decrease (16 C), and later than the MS (MS maximum at about 45 s, time constant 11 s; hippocampus peak at 115 s, time constants 48 s right and 72 s left).
outcomes.source: Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 3; Figure S1H to K
outcomes.quote: found < 1.5° C decrease in the hippocampus at the time of the largest MS temperature decrease (16° C) ... (maximum effect at approximately 45 s; time constant: 11 s), the mild temperature decrease in the hippocampus was considerably delayed (peak at 115 s; time constant 48 s for the right hippocampus, and 72 s for the left)
outcomes.notes: The control experiment with MS and hippocampal temperature (Figure S1H to K) is not in the dandiset: the files hold only the septal probe's measured temperature or the lab's modelled curve, and no epoch is a temperature control session. It is not public elsewhere as far as the paper says (no other repository is named).

findings.statement: Measured MS temperature traces hold artefacts far outside any brain temperature, with no description of them: raw values up to 1354 C (MS21-180625), 1276 C (MS22-180720) and 801 C (MS21-180803) and down to -1751 C (MS22-180712) and -257 C (MS22-180623); 11 of the 31 measured traces hold values outside 5 to 45 C, and three MS22 traces hold values near 5 and 10 C outside the trials.

The 2018-07-19 sessions of MS21 and MS22 are labelled as cooled (cooling intervals and Cooling trials), but their measured MS temperature does not fall below 37.4 and 35.2 C. In MS22-180719 theta frequency still falls during the labelled cooling (8.68 to 8.27 Hz), in MS21-180719 it rises (7.53 to 8.13 Hz).

Twenty sessions have no measured MS temperature, only the lab's modelled curve (all MS10 sessions, 7 of 9 MS12 sessions, 2 of 5 MS13, MS21-180627 and MS22-180628), so 31 of 51 sessions support temperature analyses and MS10 none.

The hippocampal temperature of the paper's control experiment (Figure S1H to K), unit waveforms, and the paper's place fields are not in the dandiset. 23 of the 51 sessions hold no curated units, and 5 hold units without a cell type.

Thirteen sessions have two cooling epochs; in MS12-170717 and MS12-170718 the second cooling interval ends at 25683 s and 28409 s, long after the last trial, and four sessions have a no-cooling interval that ends before it starts (left out by the conversion, as its description says).

The lab's theta channel of MS13-171130 (channel 82) is marked bad in the electrodes table. The epochs table names the environment Linear_Track_Peter for theta maze epochs (paradigm ThetaMaze_AlternativeRunning) in 2 sessions, such as MS21-180629.

Five of the paper's 53 behavioural sessions are not in the dandiset (MS12-170712, MS13-171204, MS13-171205, MS13-171206 and MS21-180806). The release notes of version 0.261115.0311 name the first four as not in the dandiset and do not mention MS21-180806.

In MS21-180621 and MS22-180621 the good units carry no more spatial information than with their spikes shifted by 60 s (median 0.170 and 0.119 bits/spike, against 0.214 and 0.152 shifted), while in MS21-180625 and MS22-180629 the information falls from 0.842 and 1.037 to 0.061 and 0.083 bits/spike with the shift. The clock of spikes and position could not be established in these two sessions.

The dandiset holds three sessions that are outside the paper's behavioural analysis (MS21-180719, MS22-180719 and MS10-170307) without saying so. The 2018-07-19 files say that the septum does not appear to have been cooled, and MS10-170307 has Pre, Cooling and Post trials like the analysed sessions.
The Methods give position tracking at 120 Hz; six MS10 sessions are tracked at 40 Hz, one at 30 Hz and two at 119.8 Hz. The release notes say that MS10's 120 Hz OptiTrack files were not converted.

outcomes.note: A change in the claims file and in the sessions. The earlier attempt used the 45 sessions of a list from the paper's unlinked code, which leaves out MS10-170307; the rewritten claims file drops that list, and the blind attempt uses all 51 sessions, where MS10-170307 has 37 trials, outside 72 to 220. The mean (143.8 and 142.4) and the median pre trials (39 in both) agree.

A difference in method. The earlier attempt used the code's aligned series of 198 positions over 37 sessions (R = 0.789); the blind attempt averages trials -40 to 80 over 29 to 31 sessions (120 points), which smooths more and gives R = 0.978, above the tolerance. The dataset also changed, as version 0.261115.0311 marks 11 series outside MS10 as modelled, so the blind attempt uses 31 measured sessions where the earlier one used 37.

A difference in the power measure, which the rewritten claims file leaves open with readings. The earlier attempt took the code's spectrogram magnitude at frames above 30 cm/s minus each session's mean (R = -0.056); the blind attempt takes the mean squared Hilbert amplitude over the trial (R = 0.495), and 3 of its 18 measure and reading combinations meet the criterion.

A difference in the power measure. Both find frequency lower during cooling than before and after; the earlier attempt found power not lower than post (P = 0.94) with the code's spectrogram measure, and the blind attempt finds it lower with the spectral peak power (P = 3.2e-6) but not with the Hilbert power (P = 0.42).

A change in the claims file. Its reading (c) is now the largest decrease of the aligned mean series, which gives 11.1% in the blind attempt; under the mean per-session readings both attempts find about 9% (8.88 to 9.23% and 6.6 to 9.9%).

A difference in the power measure. The earlier attempt used the code's spectrogram power and found one rat (MS10); the blind attempt uses per-session normalised Hilbert power and finds MS13 and MS21, with 3 rats under raw Hilbert power and 1 under spectral power.

A difference in the sessions. The earlier attempt used 15 of the code's 18 Figure 5 sessions, and its cooling speed was 0.3 cm/s below the tolerance under reading (b); the blind attempt uses the 23 sessions with place cell pairs, which the added curated units of version 0.261115.0311 make possible, and finds 80.3 and 77.1 cm/s, both within tolerance.

A change in the claims file, which now carries the 14% decrease of Figure S2D. Both attempts find a significant decrease of interneuron oscillation frequency (9.4% earlier, 8.7% in the blind attempt), neither within 12.6 to 15.4%.

A difference in method. The earlier attempt measured size on each state's map within 4 bins of the field found on running frames, over 635 fields, with R = 0.8197 at the edge of the tolerance; the blind attempt measures contiguous bins above 10% of the state's peak on maps of all frames, over 1193 fields with cell types from the files, and finds R = 0.465.

A difference in method, the field and size definitions of fig3c-field-size-correlated. The earlier attempt found R pre 0.246 (P = 4.7e-06); the blind attempt finds pre R between -0.032 and 0.059 under its readings.

A change in the claims file, which now fixes 10 cm/s speed bins with 20 cm/s as a variant. The earlier attempt used 20 cm/s bins and found fp lower during cooling in every bin it could test; the blind attempt finds it lower in 11 of 14 bins of 10 cm/s and in 8 of 8 bins of 20 cm/s.

A change in the claims file, which now requires the surface fit of the Methods. The earlier attempt measured compression by a regression of lag on distance (0.273 cm/ms); the blind attempt found that the surface fit does not fit the density under either reading of the equation and blocked the claim as methods_underspecified.

A difference in the pairs. Both find cooling lags longer than pre and post; the blind attempt has 8506 pairs against 3136, from fields on maps over all trials and the added curated units of version 0.261115.0311, and with them pre and post also differ (P = 0.034, earlier P = 0.0967).

A difference in the pairs. Both take the largest peak within pi of zero and compare absolute lags; the earlier attempt found cooling lags larger than pre (P = 0.0015), and the blind attempt, with 8451 pairs from fields on maps over all trials and the cell types and added curated units of version 0.261115.0311, finds no change (P = 0.37). The blind attempt's nearest-peak reading gives a change (P = 2.7e-8), so the outcome rests on how the lag is read.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2: the full executed notebook of the revision after round 1, with its conclusions and Summary, the helper module, the README, the attempt record and the claims file, with the paper. Its report is transcripts/petersen-2020/verifier-2-report.md. It agreed with all 46 outcomes. Its points on the data check and the Summary, which concern no single claim, were answered as follows: the behaviour descriptions give 120, 40 or 30 Hz and match the timestamps in every session (now printed per session), so the tracking-rate metadata_error is withdrawn and cell 5 and the Summary corrected; the raw temperature range (-1751 to 1354 C), the theta frequencies of the 2018-07-19 sessions and the end of the second cooling interval of MS12-170717 and MS12-170718 are now printed in the data check.

paper_notes.statement: The paper reports 53 sessions in 5 rats and subsets of 21, 19, 18 and 10 sessions, and 365 place fields, without naming them; the dandiset holds 51 sessions, so the subsets cannot be matched.

Question for the authors: which peak of a pair's phase cross-correlogram is its phase lag (Figure 5I)? The largest peak within pi of zero gives no change with cooling (P >= 0.37), the peak nearest zero a change (P = 2.7e-8); the attempt assumed the first.

The surface equation of the Methods (Spatial temporal compression) has lost its fraction bars in the available text, and the preparation of the density, the grid, start values and fitting procedure are not given. Under both readings the equation's oscillation term takes the density to zero between ridges, while the density's theta modulation is about 4 to 7% of its level, and the fits, also bounded and from several starts, explain less than the density's mean, so the compression of Figure 5C and G could not be measured (fig5cg blocked). The fitting code would let it be repeated.

Question for the authors: on which rate map were the place fields of Figure 5 found by the automatic rule (the map over all trials, over control trials, or per state)? The attempt assumed the map over all trials of an arm, so that each field has the same boundaries in every state; the outcomes of the place field claims rest on it.
Place fields of Figures 3 and 4 were defined by hand; the field boundaries, or the list of the 365 fields, would let the field claims be tested on the paper's fields.

Question for the authors: within what range was the circular-linear regression slope of phase precession searched (Figure 4D, S3E)? With a range of 1 cycle per field about 30% of the slopes sit at the bound and no change with cooling is found; with 2 cycles, the attempt's assumption, precession is flatter during cooling than before (P = 0.016) but not than after (P = 0.073), and without the slopes at the bound neither comparison is significant.

The legend of Figure 5H gives P = 8.0e-5 by a sign rank test with N = 10 sessions; an exact signed-rank test over 10 sessions cannot give a P below 0.00195, so the test must be over pairs or the N refers to something else.
The Discussion gives a 12% decrease of LFP theta frequency during cooling, while the Results give within-field LFP theta of 8.4 Hz before and 7.7 Hz during cooling, a decrease of 8.3%.

entries.title: Cooling of the medial septum and hippocampal theta coordination (Petersen and Buzsaki 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Petersen and Buzsaki (2020) on dandiset 000059, which holds 51 sessions of 5 rats running a figure-8 maze while the medial septum was cooled, with CA1 LFP, curated units, head tracking and the septal temperature. It tests the effects of cooling on theta frequency and power, choice errors, running speed, place cell rates, oscillation frequency, field features, phase precession and the theta time and phase lags of place cell pairs. The hippocampal temperature of the paper's control experiment is not in the dandiset.
